definitions.explanation: A building constructed with five stories. A standard example of the 〜{階|かい}{建|だ}て counter pattern, which describes how many floors a building has.

examples.japanese: {五階建|ごかいだ}てのアパートだ。
{駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しい{五階建|ごかいだ}てのビルが{建|た}った。
examples.english: A new five-story building went up in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{五階建|ごかいだ}ての{団地|だんち}にはエレベーターがないことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Old five-story housing complexes often don't have elevators.

notes:
Compound of {五|ご} (five) + {階|かい} (floor counter) + {建|だ}て (constructed). One member of the productive 〜{階|かい}{建|だ}て pattern.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {五階建|ごかいだ}てのアパート: five-story apartment building
- {五階建|ごかいだ}てのビル: five-story building
- {五階建|ごかいだ}ての{団地|だんち}: five-story public housing

RELATED PATTERNS:
- {二|に}{階|かい}{建|だ}て: two-story
- {三|さん}{階|かい}{建|だ}て: three-story
- {高層|こうそう}{階|かい}{建|だ}て / {高層|こうそう}ビル: high-rise building
- {平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}て: single-story (irregular — no {階|かい})

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many older Japanese {団地|だんち} (public housing complexes) built in the 1960s-70s are five-story walk-ups, since buildings up to five floors were not required by law to have elevators.
